subject: Re: Privacy Questionnaire — Access zoning, PII handling & transfer clarifications
messages:
From: Lena Moore <lena.moore@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security <security@acmehealth.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: Privacy questionnaire and architecture diagram request

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of our vendor risk review we'll need a completed privacy/security questionnaire and a high-level dataflow diagram that shows how PII moves through Redwood's systems (ingest, tokenization/pseudonymization, KV cache, logs/telemetry, backups). I have attached the Acme_SSQ_v2.xlsx with our question set.

Specifically we'd like answers to:
- Which categories of PII you classify (PII, Sensitive PI, Health Data) and where that classification is stored
- Whether any plaintext PII is persisted beyond 30 days and where
- KMS custody model (do you hold keys, customer KMS options, HSM attestations)
- Subprocessors that handle request logs, telemetry, backups, and who has access to decrypted payloads
- Any cross-border transfer mechanisms and standard contractual clauses used (if applicable)

Could you return the completed SSQ and a diagram by EOD Friday our time? If you need an initial call, propose 30 minutes and we'll find a slot.

Attachments: Acme_SSQ_v2.xlsx (questionnaire)

Best,
Lena Moore
Director, Vendor Security
AcmeHealth

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Lena Moore <lena.moore@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Privacy questionnaire and architecture diagram request

Hi Lena —

Thanks, we've started filling the SSQ and sketched the requested dataflow. Please find attached our completed answers (redwood_ssq_answers_20280517.pdf) and a simplified architecture diagram (redwood_dataflow_v1.vsdx). Key notes up front:

- PII classification: We store classification metadata in our control plane (no PII stored there). Categories we reference: Identifiers, Contact Info, Credentials, Health-related Text (tagged as Sensitive PI).
- Retention: No plaintext PII persisted beyond 30 days by default in hosted deployments; customers can configure retention for Dedicated/Private.
- KMS: Customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we use customer-specific envelope keys when requested, otherwise we manage keys in a multi-tenant KMS with HSM-backed providers. See attached attestation references.
- Subprocessors: We provided a short inventory covering telemetry processors, logging providers, and backup storage. Detailed CSV attached in follow-up.
- Cross-border transfers: We employ SCCs for EU transfers and can restrict region residency on Dedicated/Private.

If possible let's set a 30-minute clarifying call on Friday 16:30 ET / 13:30 PT. Marissa and Aditya are looped for the attestation and subprocessor inventory.

Attachments: redwood_ssq_answers_20280517.pdf, redwood_dataflow_v1.vsdx

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Lena Moore <lena.moore@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 15:42:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Privacy questionnaire and architecture diagram request

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifications after an internal review:

1) KMS custody: In your answers you mention "multi-tenant KMS with HSM-backed providers" for hosted. Can you confirm whether Redwood personnel ever have access to plaintext payload keys in hosted mode? If so, what controls and access review cadence apply?

2) Telemetry and logs: We need to understand which processors ingest request-level telemetry and whether request payloads are redacted prior to leaving your environment. The SSQ asks for an example of a retention timeline for logs that contain identifiers.

3) Evidence: Can you provide your latest KMS attestation and a current subprocessor inventory file with vendor roles? We'll need those artifacts to advance the security board review.

We can take the call but would prefer a short written response to the three points above before the meeting so we can triage internally.

Thanks,
Lena

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lena Moore <lena.moore@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Privacy questionnaire and architecture diagram request

Hi Lena — looping in the artifacts and answers to your three items. Quoting Jordan's original points where helpful.

On KMS custody and operator access:
- For Hosted: we use a tenant-isolated envelope encryption approach. Customer request payloads are encrypted with ephemeral data keys; those keys are wrapped by a tenant-specific master key. For customers who do not provide their own KMS, Redwood operates the wrapping keys in an HSM-backed cloud KMS. Redwood engineers do not have routine access to unwrap customer data keys. Access to KMS unwrap operations is gated by an IAM workflow and requires an approval ticket plus recorded justification (access reviews monthly).

On telemetry, logs, and retention:
- Request payloads are redacted prior to export for telemetry. Telemetry contains hashed request IDs and high-level token metrics; we do not ship full plaintext prompts.
- Logs that may contain identifiers (rare debug captures) are retained for 30 days by default and scrubbed; customers can request shorter retention or opt-out of certain telemetry categories on Dedicated/Private.

Evidence and inventory (attached):
- kms-attestation.pdf (signed KMS attestation covering HSM provider and control assertions)
- subprocessor-inventory.csv (vendor, function, region, access type). Key subprocessors handling telemetry/logging/backups are listed and marked where they receive tokenized vs. plaintext data.

Related links: drive folder with full evidence: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Gx-example-drive-link; HubSpot record HS-4785123 contains the procurement/contract stub.

If you'd like a call to walk through the artifacts we're available Friday 16:30 ET / 13:30 PT or Monday morning. Let us know what works for the Acme security board.

Attachments: kms-attestation.pdf, subprocessor-inventory.csv

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security & Privacy Program Manager
Redwood Inference
